name: San Pedro de Cardeña monastery (International Brigades camp)
story: The ancient monastery near Burgos, traditionally linked to El Cid, was turned into a concentration camp in December 1936. From April 1938 it was the main camp for captured International Brigaders, held alongside Spanish prisoners, until it closed in November 1939. British, Irish, American and other volunteers taken at Jarama, Belchite, Calaceite and Gandesa passed through; some were exchanged, others transferred to prisons. Army psychiatrist Antonio Vallejo-Nágera carried out pseudo-scientific studies on inmates here aiming to identify a 'Marxist' psychological type. Memoirs by former prisoners describe hunger, beatings and forced saluting.
see: The restored monastery church and cloister, today home to a Cistercian (Trappist) community; there is no major memorial to the prisoners.
plan: 10 km southeast of Burgos; visits are guided by a monk at set times — check monastery hours. Please be discreet: it is an active monastery.
